title: Leave a walking frame ready before he stands: square in front, open side toward him
instruction: Mr Okafor is about to stand up from his armchair and walk with his walking frame. Leave the frame ready for him: standing on its four feet directly in front of him and centred on him, square to his chair, with its open side toward him and its back legs 10 to 50 mm (8 to 40 cm at this 1:8 scale) in front of his toes.
context: Nursing assistants, personal care aides and physical therapist aides (O*NET 31-1131.00, 31-1122.00, 31-2022.00) get residents up from their chairs many times a day. A resident who walks with a frame is taught to stand by pushing up on the chair's arms, not by pulling on the frame, which can tip toward him, and then to take the frame's handgrips. So the frame is left ready before he stands: on its four feet directly in front of his chair, square to it, its open side toward him so that he stands inside it, and a short step from his toes, near enough to take once he is up but clear of his feet. A frame left beside the chair, out of reach or turned crossbar toward him makes him reach, twist or set off without it, which falls-prevention programmes in care homes warn against. The 8 to 40 cm band is a set-up rule of thumb, stated in the instruction.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height and stands for the floor of a care-home lounge at 1:8 scale. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Below, x and y are in cm and heights above the table in mm. Fixed to the table: (1) Armchair, green upholstered wooden blocks, facing the arms: seat x 39.5-45.5, y -3.4 to +3.4, 0-55 mm; backrest x 45.5-47.0, y -4.4 to +4.4, 0-110; two arms x 39.5-45.5, y +3.4 to +4.4 and -4.4 to -3.4, 0-75. (2) Mr Okafor, a rigid seated manikin of painted 3D-printed PLA blocks, in the chair facing the arms (facing -x), so his right side is toward +y; his centre line is at y 0. His parts are boxes: maroon slippers x 35.0-38.5, y +0.3 to +1.8 and -1.8 to -0.3, 0-9 mm (his toes on the line x 35.0); charcoal shins x 37.3-38.5, y +0.4 to +1.7 and -1.7 to -0.4, 9-55; charcoal thighs x 37.3-43.0, y -1.9 to +1.9, 55-69; beige torso x 43.0-45.5, y -2.2 to +2.2, 55-115; beige upper arms x 44.3-45.5, y +2.2 to +3.4 and -3.4 to -2.2, 83-112; brown forearms resting on the chair's arms, x 40.5-45.0, y +3.5 to +4.3 and -4.3 to -3.5, 75-83; and the head, a brown 26 mm sphere centred at x 44.2, y 0, 128 mm up. Loose: (3) Walking frame: one rigid 60 g model of aluminium 8 x 8 mm square tube (no moving parts), 56 mm deep, 70 mm across (outer faces of its legs) and 106 mm tall. Its front is the crossbar side; its back is open. Positions below are forward of (+) or behind (-) the middle of its footprint. Four legs at the footprint's corners, each a grey rubber ferrule 0-10 mm up under an aluminium tube to 98 mm. Two top rails, one each side, 56 mm long (-28 to +28 mm), 98-106 mm up, each with a black foam handgrip over its middle 32 mm (-16 to +16 mm). A lower side rail on each side between its two legs, 40 mm long, 50-58 mm up. One crossbar between the front legs, 54 mm long, 70-78 mm up. Nothing joins the back legs. It stands on its four ferrules with its footprint centre at x 30.0, y -17.0 (to his left front, out of his reach), side-on to him: its crossbar toward -y, its open side toward +y (toward the midline). Its footprint covers x 26.5-33.5, y -19.8 to -14.2. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from the frame's pose at the last step, as a top photo with a protractor and a rule would read it. Footprint: the 56 x 70 mm rectangle round the outer faces of its four legs. Turn: the angle seen from above between the frame's forward direction (from its open side to its crossbar) and -x (toward the arms, away from him): 0 = square, open side toward him; 90 = side-on (as it starts); 180 = crossbar toward him. Off-centre: how far the footprint's centre is from his centre line (y 0), along y. Toe gap d: from his toe line (x 35.0 cm, the front of his slippers) to the footprint corner nearest it, along x (square, its back legs); negative = a leg past the line, round his feet. 'Set down': each of its four feet has its lowest point within 3 mm of the floor (standing on all four, not tipped onto two, not lifted more than 3 mm) and it is still (its footprint centre's path, turns counted at its corners, under 5 mm over the last 0.5 s). Each of three conditions has a full band and a loose band, edges included: square, turn 15 degrees or less (loose: up to 30); centred, off-centre 20 mm or less (loose: up to 50 mm); distance, d 10 to 50 mm, 8 to 40 cm at scale (loose: 0 to under 10, or over 50 to 100 mm). Score 0 if the frame is not set down (lifted, tipped, on its side, upside down, still moving), or any condition is outside its loose band: turned more than 30 degrees (side-on, or crossbar toward him), more than 50 mm off his centre line (beside the chair), a leg past his toe line (round his feet) or more than 100 mm from his toes. Otherwise, counting the conditions only in their loose band: none 1.0; one 0.5; two 0.25; all three 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Examples: square, centred and 30 mm from his toes 1.0; the same but turned 20 degrees, or 35 mm off centre, or 70 mm or 5 mm from his toes, 0.5; turned 20 degrees and 35 mm off centre, or 35 mm off centre and 70 mm away, 0.25; turned 20 degrees, 35 mm off centre and 70 mm away 0; side-on or crossbar toward him at any place 0; 60 mm off centre 0; 120 mm away 0; round his feet 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. In a real trial, read the turn with a protractor on a top photo against a line along y, and d and the off-centre distance with a rule square to the toe line.
fidelity: 1:8 scale (a frame 560 mm across, 450 mm deep, 850 mm tall). Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The chair and manikin are fixed; he does not move or stand. The frame is one rigid body of seventeen boxes: no height adjustment or folding. The scorer sees only the frame, so a frame held still within 3 mm of the floor counts as set down. The 8-40 cm band is a set-up rule of thumb stated as the instruction's rule, not a cited standard.
reset_notes: Stand the walking frame on its four feet with its footprint centre at x 30.0 cm, y -17.0 cm, side-on: its crossbar toward -y (the robot's right), its open side toward +y. The armchair and manikin are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
